s1.syndrome_frame: Facial asymmetry with possible cranial nerve involvement in a neonate
salient_findings: Enhancing mass in the left cerebellopontine angle and internal auditory canal on MRI
Profound hearing loss in the left ear on auditory brainstem response testing
key_facts: 4-week-old male patient
Left facial asymmetry observed during crying
Passed infant hearing screening previously
MRI showed an enhancing mass in the left cerebellopontine angle and internal auditory canal
Follow-up MRI showed considerable growth of the mass
Auditory brainstem response testing demonstrated profound hearing loss in the left ear
Histopathological examination revealed a vascular lesion with low levels of mitotic activity
Biphasic lesion composed of vascular nodules among spindle cells
Glomeruloid-like architecture of vascular epithelial nodules
Ki-67 labeling index: 5% to 10%
CD34 and CD31 positive for endothelial cells

shortlist.label: Hemangioma
shortlist.why_kept: MRI showed an enhancing mass, histopathological examination revealed a vascular lesion

shortlist.label: Lymphangioma
shortlist.why_kept: Histopathological examination showed a biphasic lesion with glomeruloid-like architecture, similar to lymphangiomatosis

shortlist.label: Lymphangiomatosis
shortlist.why_kept: Histopathological examination revealed a pattern similar to lymphangiomatosis

shortlist.label: Kaposiform hemangioendothelioma
shortlist.why_kept: Vascular lesion with low levels of mitotic activity, CD34 and CD31 positive for endothelial cells

shortlist.label: Cranial nerve schwannoma
shortlist.why_kept: Mass located in the left cerebellopontine angle and internal auditory canal, profound hearing loss in the left ear

raw.rationale: The presence of a vascular lesion with low levels of mitotic activity, biphasic lesion composed of vascular nodules among spindle cells, and glomeruloid-like architecture of vascular epithelial nodules, along with positive CD34 and CD31 staining for endothelial cells, are consistent with hemangioma. The initial presentation of left facial asymmetry and subsequent profound hearing loss in the left ear can be explained by the location of the mass in the left cerebellopontine angle and internal auditory canal.

rejected.label: Lymphangioma
rejected.why: While the histopathological pattern is similar to lymphangiomatosis, the presence of CD34 and CD31 positive endothelial cells and the glomeruloid-like architecture suggests a hemangioma rather than a lymphangioma.

rejected.label: Lymphangiomatosis
rejected.why: Lymphangiomatosis typically involves multiple lesions and has a more complex clinical presentation, which is not consistent with the single mass and clinical findings in this case.

rejected.label: Kaposiform hemangioendothelioma
rejected.why: Kaposiform hemangioendothelioma typically presents with more aggressive features, such as Kasabach-Merritt syndrome, and has a distinct histological appearance that is not described in this case.

rejected.label: Cranial nerve schwannoma
rejected.why: The histopathological findings do not support a diagnosis of schwannoma, as there is no mention of S-100 positive spindle cells or a characteristic Antoni A and Antoni B pattern.
